title: The wood’s own brother helps cut it
odia:
କାଠ କହିଲା- ମୋତେ କିଏ ହାଣୁଚି ?
ତୋ’ ଭାଇ ତା ଭିତରେ ପଶି ହାଣୁଚି।
literal_meaning: The wood asked, “Who is cutting me?” “Your brother has entered it and is cutting you.”
meaning_odia: ନିଜ ପକ୍ଷର ଜଣେ ବିରୋଧୀଙ୍କ ସହ ମିଶି ନିଜ ଲୋକଙ୍କ କ୍ଷତି କରାଇବାର କଥା। କୁରାଢ଼ିରେ ଲାଗିଥିବା କାଠ ବେଣ୍ଟକୁ କାଠର ଭାଇ ବୋଲି ଦେଖିଲେ ଉପମାଟି ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ ହୁଏ—ନିଜ ଜାତିର ଜିନିଷ ହିଁ ଆଘାତର ସାଧନକୁ ସାହାଯ୍ୟ କରୁଛି।
explanation: The inspected public variant makes the axe the respondent and explains the saying as harm enabled by someone from one’s own side. The wooden handle supplies the natural reading of the wood’s brother: something akin to the victim has become part of the instrument that hurts it.
usage_example: A member secretly gives a rival group the information needed to undermine a shared project. The others use the saying to describe the help the rival received from within. This illustration is newly composed.
cultural_context: The little dialogue personifies wood and turns shared material into kinship. Calling the handle a brother makes the injury more pointed: the cutting depends on wood’s own kind. The longer public form names the axe, while the upload leaves that part implicit.

witnesses.locator: Page10, two-line dialogue beginning କାଠ କହିଲା.
witnesses.note: Rendered page inspected17November2026. Concise wording retained, with unnamed respondent and ତା ଭିତରେ.
Expanded dialogue names କୁରାଢ଼ି as respondent and says ମୋ ଭିତରେ; explicit gloss concerns one’s own member helping an enemy harm the group. Not exact uploaded wording.

origin_note: Upload attests the concise displayed wording; Odia Vasa gives an expanded dialogue and explicit gloss. Their relationship and earliest circulation remain unknown.

odia_summary: ନିଜ ପକ୍ଷର ଲୋକ ବିରୋଧୀଙ୍କୁ ସାହାଯ୍ୟ କରି ନିଜ ଲୋକଙ୍କ କ୍ଷତି କରାଇବା।
english_summary: Harm from outside is enabled by someone from within.
